title: Predicting Physical Properties of Yellowballs
text:
🔬 In Progress
    Predicting Physical Properties of Yellowballs
    Math 4025 — Statistical Machine Learning · Spring 2026 · Target: SURF_DENS (Surface Mass Density)
  
  

  
  
    
      👩‍💻 Zaynab
      👤 Maddie
      👤 Aiden
    
    ⬡ GitHub Repo
    Slides / Report
  

  
  
    
      🌌 Project Overview
      
        "Yellowballs" are compact, roughly circular structures in the Milky Way first identified by
        citizen scientists via the Milky Way Project. They are candidate sites of intermediate- to
        high-mass star formation, appearing "yellow" due to the wavelengths they emit most strongly.
        The MIRION catalog (Wolf-Chase et al. 2025) contains 6,176 Yellowballs with photometric
        measurements from the Spitzer and Herschel space telescopes.
      
      
        Our team is building a machine learning pipeline to predict surface mass density
        (SURF_DENS, g/cm²) — the total gas and dust mass per unit area — from each
        Yellowball's infrared photometric signature. Accurate predictions would allow astronomers
        to characterize newly discovered objects without time-intensive follow-up observations.
      
    
    
      
        Problem Type
        Regression
      
      
        Target Variable
        SURF_DENS (g/cm²)
      
      
        Dataset
        MIRION catalog · 3,945 labeled samples
      
      
        Distance Dependent?
        No ✅
      
    
  

  
  🔭 Scientific Context
  
  
    
      Photometry measures how bright an object appears at specific wavelengths of light. Each
      wavelength measurement (called a flux density) is recorded by a telescope filter,
      and together these form a spectral energy distribution (SED) — a kind of
      fingerprint encoding information about an object's physical properties like temperature,
      mass, and luminosity.
    
    
      Our features come from two telescopes. Spitzer provides shorter-wavelength
      bands (8, 12, 24 µm), and Herschel provides longer-wavelength bands
      (70, 160, 250, 350, 500, 870, 1100 µm). The 70 µm band is particularly interesting: it
      comes from Herschel but was incorporated directly alongside the Spitzer bands in MIRION,
      and shorter-wavelength bands (including 70 µm) are generally considered more predictive.
    
    
      A key research question is: can we make accurate predictions using only the 2–70 µm
      wavelengths? And which specific wavelengths drive the predictions most?
    
  

  
  🛠 Tech Stack
  
  
    Python
    scikit-learn
    pandas
    NumPy
    Matplotlib / Seaborn
    missingno
    Quarto (.qmd)
    GitHub Actions
  

  
  📋 Progress
  
  
    

      
        ✅
        Target Variable SelectedAssigned SURF_DENS; confirmed it is distance-independent (no distance file needed).
      

      
        ✅
        Repository SetupGitHub Classroom repo cloned; team name set to target variable.
      

      
        ✅
        Data Loading & JoiningLoaded MIRION_meta_all_1.csv and MIRION_spec_1.csv; joined on YB identifier.
      

      
        ✅
        EDA — Target & FeaturesIn progress — plotting SURF_DENS distribution, flux band distributions, and scatter plots of each band vs. target. Checking missing values with missingno.
      

      
        🔄
        Baseline ModelPlanned — linear regression on the four Spitzer bands (F8, F12, F24, F70) with cross-validation to establish benchmark R² and RMSE.
      

      
        ⏳
        Feature Engineering & IterationPlanned — add flux ratios, long-wavelength bands, quality flag indicators; try ensemble models; tune hyperparameters.
      

      
        ⏳
        Final Evaluation & InterpretationPlanned — cross-validated R² and RMSE; feature importance analysis; astrophysical interpretation of which wavelengths matter most.
      

      
        ⏳
        Presentation & Executive SummaryDue April 30 — 7-minute talk + 1–2 page summary for astronomy researcher audience.
      

    

    
    
      
        Overall progress~35%
      
      
        
      
    
  

  
  👥 Team Roles
  
  
    
      👩‍💻
      Zaynab
   
    
    
      👤
      Maddie
      
    
    
      👤
      Aiden
     
    
  

  
  📈 Key Findings So Far
  
  
    
      We'll update this section as results come in. Initial EDA is underway. We'll report on the
      distribution of SURF_DENS, any skewness or outliers, missing value patterns across flux bands,
      and early correlations between photometric features and surface density.

title: Cover Letter
text:

      Hiring Team
      Quintrix Solutions
      Union, NJ
    

    Dear Hiring Team,

    
      I am writing to express my strong interest in the Junior Data Engineer position at Quintrix Solutions.
      As a Computer Science and Mathematics student at The College of Idaho graduating in May 2026 with
      hands-on experience in Python, SQL, cloud infrastructure, and CI/CD pipelines. I am excited by the
      opportunity to grow into a data engineering role through Quintrix's structured training pathway.
    

    
      My most recent role as a Software Engineering Intern at Schweitzer Engineering Laboratories gave me
      direct experience building Python-based automation scripts and working within a production CI/CD
      environment using Jenkins and GitHub Actions. Prior to that, I interned at SWCA Environmental
      Consultants, where I developed RESTful APIs using Python and FastAPI, designed data ingestion
      workflows to extract and transform structured data, and containerized applications using Docker. These 
      skills map directly to the ETL and deployment responsibilities in this role. I also hold an
      AWS Cloud Practitioner certification and have hands-on experience with EC2, S3, Lambda, and RDS.
    

    
      On the data side, I have worked extensively with SQL across PostgreSQL and MySQL, including writing
      complex joins, subqueries, and aggregations. One project I am particularly proud of is a relational
      database system I designed for a simulated college environment: I modeled entity relationships
      using UML, applied normalization rules, and wrote analytical queries for reporting and
      decision-making — all skills directly relevant to database design and optimization work at Quintrix.
    

    
      Beyond technical skills, I bring strong teamwork and communication habits developed through two
      internships, a teaching assistant role, and leading the largest cultural organization on my campus.
      I am a fast learner who is genuinely excited about deepening my knowledge of data engineering,
      DevOps, and cloud technologies through the structured training Quintrix provides.
    

    
      I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my background aligns with this role. Thank you for
      your time and consideration — I look forward to hearing from you.
    

    
      Sincerely,
      Zaynab El Hakour
